note: Adapted from the original English description of Scheffrahn & Křeček 1999, where the species was established as Cryptotermes aequacornis n. sp.; type locality rain forest in the mountains south of La Vache Bay, Trinidad, known from a single colony. The original explicitly states 'Imago. Unknown.' under the alate heading, so this entry has only a soldier section. The original describes the head colour pattern as the 'anterior 1/3' and the 'posterior 1/3'; the fraction signs are damaged in the photocopy text layer (printed as 113, 112 and the like), and the proportions are restored here as described in the original; the measurements are transcribed from the original plate (p. 127, Table 2), 6 individuals. The name refers to the frontal horns and genal horns being almost identical in shape and size.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule, in dorsal view, almost black on the anterior third and grading to rusty orange over the posterior third; in lateral view the anterior half of the head almost black and the posterior half rusty orange. Mandibles very dark chestnut brown. Anterior margin of the pronotum rusty, the remainder with a paler broad border. Head slightly elongate, the sides almost parallel and slightly concave in the middle, the posterior part broadly rounded; a deep pit in the middle of the vertex. Anterior part (including the frontal margin and the frontal face) with deep rugae. Frontal face deeply concave. Frontal margin stout, especially prominent in frontal view, with a deep median notch connected to the median vertex pit; in dorsal view the frontal margin straight or only very shallowly incised. Vertex face meeting the frontal face at about 90°. Eye spots absent or very faint, small and oval. Labrum short, pointed, the anterolateral margins slightly concave. Frontal horns large, ball-shaped. Genal horns almost the same shape and size as the frontal horns, slightly more conical; the bases of the two pairs contiguous. Mandibles very short, raised and bent in the middle, projecting horizontally in lateral view; dentition weak. Antennae 11—13-segmented, usually 11 or 12, the segment formula 2>3=4=5 or 2>3<4=5. Pronotum almost square, the sides slightly convex, the posterior margin very shallowly concave; anterior margin with a double convex incision or emargination, and weakly and irregularly undulate. Lateral margins of the mesonotum and metanotum slightly triangular.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Measurements (6 individuals, 1 colony, in mm, holotype): head length to the tip of the mandibles 1.46—1.61 (1.54±0.052, holotype 1.54); head length to the frontal horns 1.36—1.44 (1.40±0.029, 1.38); frontal margin width 1.05—1.14 (1.11±0.045, 1.06); outer span of the frontal horns 0.82—0.92 (0.87±0.038, 0.85); maximum head width 1.06—1.18 (1.12±0.045, 1.06); head height without the postmentum 0.82—0.96 (0.91±0.063, 0.82); maximum pronotal width 0.93—1.06 (1.01±0.052, 0.97); maximum pronotal length 0.75—0.82 (0.80±0.029, 0.77); left mandible length (apex to ventral articulation) 0.56—0.62 (0.60±0.029, 0.62); total body length 3.51—4.06 (3.76±0.20, 3.81). The original also compares it with C. darlingtonae: that species has a concave anterolateral corner of the head capsule and frontal horns about three times the volume of the genal horns, whereas in this species the frontal and genal horns are similar in size.
